analysis: The change is documentation-only in docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. Visible changes are the date bump (line 3) and a GLM5 reasoning-controls table update. The row is at head lines ~1147-1153, beyond the head excerpt (lines 1-325), so only the patch hunk was checked. The hunk documents that `reasoning: null` is unset, that `reasoning.summary` and `reasoning.generate_summary` accept auto/concise/detailed as no-ops, and that other reasoning members are refused. It describes a provider-side prompt-policy behavior in GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift. The implementation is outside the supplied evidence, so I did not verify it. The documented behavior is a request-parameter validation relaxation: no-op summary values are accepted and unknown members are still rejected. That is fail-closed and touches no auth, attestation, encryption, billing, or key-custody boundary. I read the visible head text (endpoint-resumption, drain, and register sections) and the base excerpt (autopilot/consent) as unchanged context. They are consistent with TB-011, TB-002, T-053, and the A-008 and A-016 contracts. Resumption is documented as non-bearer and non-granting, scoped to the originating socket, and sealed with a 4 KiB strict codec. Nothing in them weakens those boundaries. The patch excerpt is truncated, so rows beyond `reasoning.enabled` were not seen. Remaining question: whether the Swift implementation matches the new documented acceptance. It is outside this documentation diff, and a mismatch would not be a security regression. No threat-model update is needed.
